newsitem.title: INDIA: India revises 96/97 trade deficit to $4 bln-agency.
newsitem.headline: India revises 96/97 trade deficit to $4 bln-agency.

text.p: Indian Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah was quoted on Wednesday as saying the government has revised its estimate of the 1996/97 (April-March) trade deficit to about $4 billion from $2 billion.
The Press Trust of India (PTI) said Ramaiah told the news agency in an interview that the revision was mainly attributable to a larger than anticipated oil import bill.
"We have no control over the hardening oil prices in the international market," PTI quoted Ramaiah as saying.
"But we have asked the Petroleum Ministry and Oil and Natural Gas Corporation to raise domestic production to check at least volume growth of imports," he was quoted as saying.

Ramaiah said a decline in the rate of export growth during in November and December was a cause for concern but called it temporary. He expected exports in 1996/97 to grow by a little less than 10 percent over the previous fiscal year.
India's exports in April-December 1996 grew by 6.36 percent compared with the same period in 1995. But exports in December 1996 fell by 1.79 percent compared with the same month in 1995.
Analysing the reasons for the export slowdown, Ramaiah said industry was guided largely by profitability, notably in view of the growing domestic market.
He cited exporters' claims that the minimum alternate tax (MAT) on corporations has eroded export profits.
He also noted the high cost of export credit, a slowdown in global demand and declining industrial growth, mainly in the consumer goods sector.
Ramaiah said "avoidable delays and high transaction costs at the time of securing export-import related clearance from various regulatory authorities" were also factors in the export slowdown.
